purpose: Closed-world regression truth for the released rule set over self-authored HTML-to-PDF documents with planted, construction-known defects and clean controls. Never calibration data and never external trust evidence.
splitNote: 'regression' is deliberately not one of the calibration splits of docs/validation/corpus-contract-v1.md (development, tuning, holdout); synthetic construction truth never counts as real data.
expectedAuthoredCommit: the commit that first adds this directory (git log --diff-filter=A -- corpus/public/selfauthored-v1/expected); no breaklint report of any document exists in or before it
releaseSemantics: Expectations follow the documented semantics of the breaklint release that admits this corpus (0.7.0): e.g. content in Paged.js margin boxes (running()/fixed copies) is not in the flow and is not measured by block, line or page rules (docs/limitations.md, the 'Margin-box content.' bullet; the type rules still read a running element's source text once, and SVG in a margin box is still collected); layout/orphaned-continuation-page judges a page only where its content ends; layout/unbreakable-block-too-tall correlates fragments by flow membership, not coordinates.

gate.normative: README.md, section 'How a gate consumes this' (target, page and decline semantics: section 'Targets')
steps: Read `manifest.json` and verify the SHA-256 and byte length of every file in `files`. Zero documents read is a failure, never a skip.

Run each document in its own invocation under the default profile and read the canonical JSON report. The document's exit is that invocation's exit code, and its exit reason is `documents[0].exitReason`.

If the document ended in exit 3, pass only if 3 is in `expectedExit.set` and the exit reason is `render-unstable`. A render-unstable run withholds its findings and reports no pages by design (`docs/limitations.md`), so the page and rule checks are skipped for that document. Any other exit 3 fails.
Otherwise the exit code must be in `expectedExit.set` and the report's `pages` must lie in `pages.range`, both ends included.

Then, per rule: every `mustFire` entry is matched by at least one finding; no finding matches a `mustNotFire` target; every finding is matched by a `mustFire` or `allowed` entry of its rule, or is on a measured target whose `ifMeasured` is `mustFire` (closed world); the decline counts hold as the paragraph 'Declines' under 'Targets' defines, and a measured target with `ifMeasured: mustNotFire` has no finding; no decline row of that rule carries a reason outside `permittedDeclineReasons` (rows with `ruleId: null` follow the paragraph 'Evidence-level declines'). `layout/half-empty-page` is not active in the default profile, so any finding of it fails.

expectationHistory.what: #sidetab is now a keep-together running element of fixed height 320 px in the side margin boxes (@left-middle on left pages, @right-middle on right pages), copied onto five pages; a layout/unbreakable-block-too-tall mustNotFire entry with dependsOn G-02 / WP-F1 names it.

expectationHistory.what: Per-entry dependsOn is gone from the format and from every expected file: sa13 layout/orphaned-continuation-page middle pages (E2), sa14 #parts-band (E8) and #sidetab (E15), and sa03's string-valued dependsOn on the #cap-hourly caption page. The sa03 string, which described renderer behaviour rather than a semantic dependency, now sits in that entry's 'observed' field. README section 'Release semantics' states one class rule, and manifest.json releaseSemantics repeats it verbatim. Every mustNotFire entry of a running element (widow, orphan, unbreakable-block-too-tall, heading-at-page-bottom, hyphen-across-page: 80 entries for the 16 running elements of 14 documents) and the sa13 and sa14 entries now cite that rule in why or docsBasis.

It also had no fixed schema (sa03 used a string; sa14's sidetab marker lacked basis) and no testable condition. The orchestrator decided that release semantics are stated once as a class rule and never change pass/fail for a single entry. The author chose to remove dependsOn entirely rather than keep it as an informational annotation, so there is nothing left to apply inconsistently. The README keeps the G-02/WP-F1 and G-15/WP-F4 tracing as information only.

The generic one is removed; the detailed one remains. No list of any rule in any expected file now repeats a target.
expectationHistory.why: The duplicate carried no marker, so the marker on the detailed entry had no effect; one target should have one entry.
expectationHistory.source: independent pre-run review (no breaklint output seen)

expectationHistory.what: manifest.json gate now holds only a pointer to README 'How a gate consumes this' and its five steps, copied verbatim from the README (each step string occurs unchanged in README.md). The README's step 4 now names the report field pages (DocumentReport.pages) instead of 'pagesAnalysed', which is not a report field.
expectationHistory.why: The manifest's gate summary (no exit-3-first step, 'pagesAnalysed', and a mustFire clause 'or, where the entry says so, the named decline' that no entry used) disagreed with the README, so a gate built from the manifest would have failed every allowed render-unstable exit 3 (sa16 shows residue with all three font stacks).

gate.closedWorld: per document, any finding whose rule and target are not covered by that rule's mustFire or allowed entries fails
gate.mustFire: every mustFire entry needs at least one matching finding (or, where the entry says so, the named decline)
gate.declines: every required expectedDecline must be present; a decline reason outside permittedDeclineReasons fails
gate.exit: the document's exit code must be in expectedExit.set
gate.bytes: sha256 of every document and expected file must match this manifest
gate.empty: a run that reads zero documents fails; it is never a skip

expectationHistory.source: independent pre-run review (no breaklint output seen)

expectationHistory.what: pageOf now has one grammar: {id, fragment: first | last | middle, resolvedPages, resolvedPagesByFontStack}. fragment is required and has no default. resolvedPages is the union, over the three font stacks, of the pages on which the construction probe placed those flow fragments, and a finding matches when its page (Finding.page) is in it. sa03: {"id": "cap-hourly"} becomes fragment first, resolvedPages [6, 7] (6 with the reference fonts and FreeFont, 7 with DejaVu). sa13: fragment last gives [6]; nonFinal with excludeFirst becomes middle, [3, 4, 5]; all three stacks agree. measuredPage and measuredPages are removed. sa05: the required env/forced-break decline of layout/orphaned-continuation-page, which targeted {"pageOf": {"selector": "article.recipe"}}, now targets {"document": true} with count 6. The README defines how count is checked (the matching notMeasured rows add up to it). The sa03 note now gives the nearly empty landscape pages per font stack.
expectationHistory.why: The README defined pageOf with id only, sa05 used a selector, and sa03 gave no fragment and no default existed. The canonical report has no page map (DocumentReport.pages is a count; evaluations carry no page), so 'the run's own page map' could not be resolved. Declines (notMeasured rows) carry no page at all, so a page-keyed decline target was not checkable.
expectationHistory.source: independent pre-run review (no breaklint output seen)

expectationHistory.what: The why of the artifact/local-uri mustNotFire entries sa06 {"id": "p-6-2"} and sa15 {"id": "gpx-pfad"} now says that the entry can never match, because the element has no URI-bearing attribute, and that a tool that reports the visible-text path is caught by the closed-world check. The README's id row says the same.
expectationHistory.why: Under the id semantics for artifact/local-uri (E1, E13) these controls cannot fail, which the entries did not say.
expectationHistory.source: independent pre-run review (no breaklint output seen)

expectationHistory.what: README 'Targets': the OR applies only to list-valued keys inside one target (ids, selectors, texts, except); the four lists of a rule are not OR lists. README 'Expected files' now defines occurrences (informational number of planted instances; a mustFire entry needs at least one matching finding, and a count that differs is never a failure) and count. manifest.json's 'at least one' now comes from the same README text (E18).
expectationHistory.why: 'Several entries in a list combine with OR' could be read against step 5, where every mustFire entry is required. occurrences, used by 12 mustFire entries, was undefined.
expectationHistory.previous: 'All keys of one target combine with AND; several entries in a list combine with OR'
expectationHistory.source: independent pre-run review (no breaklint output seen)

expectationHistory.what: Retroactive record of a round-1 change in c24b677: in seven document-wide mustNotFire entries the except list moved from the entry into its target. The entries are sa06 type/spaced-hyphen and type/straight-quotes, sa15 both, sa19 type/straight-quotes (except [up-p1]) and sa20 both. E3 named only the spaced-hyphen lists and only for new items. expectationHistory.source: independent pre-run review (no breaklint output seen)

expectationHistory.what: The sa14 CSS comment 'a third of the content box' now reads 'about 35 % of the 912 px content box'. Nothing else in the bytes changed. expectationHistory.what: The required env/svg-painted-bounds-unsupported declines that carry ifMeasured (halo labels via perText, <use> text via ifMeasured) now carry measuredAlternative: true. There are 7 such entries in 5 documents. The README defines them: each target is satisfied by the decline or by a measurement, and a measured target is judged as mustFire or mustNotFire according to ifMeasured, closed-world check included.
expectationHistory.why: The expected exit sets already admit the exit a tool reaches once halo labels are measured (for example sa07 {1, 4}). But a plain required decline would have failed exactly that tool. Under the new class rule the corpus must not presume which release documents the halo bound. And a finding on a clipped halo label had no mustFire or allowed entry, so the closed-world check would have rejected a correct measurement. No construction truth changes.
expectationHistory.previous: required: true without an alternative; ifMeasured informational only
expectationHistory.source: corpus author during errata round 2, applying the orchestrator's release-semantics decision (no breaklint output seen)

expectationHistory.what: README 'Targets', paragraph 'Declines', rewritten. Declines are checked by count per rule and reason, never per target. For every rule and reason with required entries, the sum of count over the document's notMeasured rows with that ruleId and reason must equal the sum of count over those entries. measuredAlternative entries are all or nothing per rule and reason: a report sum equal to the entries' total means declined; 0 means measured, and each target is judged by its ifMeasured through source-matched findings, which also count as covered for the closed-world check; any other sum fails. The README states, and the expected files satisfy, the invariant that within one rule and reason the entries are all required or all non-required, and all measuredAlternative or none. Gate step 5 now refers to 'the decline counts'. No expected value changed.
expectationHistory.why: Decline rows carry {scope, ruleId, reason, target | null, count}. Block rules pass no target, declined() sets the target to null when count > 1, halo and <use> declines are one row per SVG, and evaluations carry a sid but no source, with no sid-to-source map in the report. So the per-target matching of E19 and E26 could not be computed from the report.
expectationHistory.previous: per-target satisfaction for named targets; summed count for document and within targets; measuredAlternative per target
expectationHistory.source: independent pre-run review (no breaklint output seen)

expectationHistory.what: README defines how artifact/local-uri findings are matched. These findings carry source: null, so a uri target matches a finding whose Finding.message contains the exact string L="V", where L is the local name of uri.attribute and V is uri.value. An id target matches L="V" for any URI-bearing attribute of X or of its descendants. sa19's {"attribute": "xlink:href"} is kept, because it describes the document, and is compared by its local name href. The README records two facts checked on the static HTML: each local URI value occurs exactly once per document, and no attribute and value pair repeats. The corpus has no CSS url() reference. No expected value changed.
expectationHistory.why: src/rules/artifact/local-uri.ts:79 emits source: null. The only handle is the message `${attribute}="${rawValue}"`, and the attribute is the parse5 local name, so xlink:href is reported as href. The README's source-span semantics could not be applied to these findings.
expectationHistory.previous: id and uri targets defined over attributes, with no stated way to find them in the report
expectationHistory.source: independent pre-run review (no breaklint output seen)

expectationHistory.what: The README tracing list under 'Release semantics' names G-79 / WP-F5 (in scope for this release) as a dependency of the two documents that use float: footnote. On current builds every footnoted document exits 3 with injection-interference. Their exit sets stay {0} (sa04) and {1} (sa17) and deliberately do not admit 3.
expectationHistory.why: The dependency was not stated anywhere. Admitting 3 would turn a known defect of current builds into an allowed outcome.
expectationHistory.source: independent pre-run review (no breaklint output seen)

expectationHistory.what:
Every mustFire entry of layout/unbreakable-block-too-tall on a block split into three or more fragments was checked against the WP-F3 round 2 content-extent lower bound (text lines and replaced content) and its flow-hazard declines. Three entries hold and stay mustFire, each with an underContentExtentLowerBound field:
- sa02 #safety-checklist: no hazard; at least (97 - 2 - 3) x 24 = 2208 px against 912 px.
- sa03 #fig-hourly: no hazard; the 700 px SVG alone against 680.31 px.
- sa09 #fig-listing-3: no hazard; at least (131 - 2 - 3) x 18 = 2268 px against 971.34 px.
Two entries are flagged and move from mustFire to allowed, class documented-gap, constructionTruth defect, each with a required: false env/invalid-measurement decline:
- sa12 #members-roll: its rows have six cells (flow hazard table-columns).
- sa14 #parts-band: li .qty { float: right } (flow hazard float).
sa12's expectedExit becomes {1, 3, 4} and sa14's {1, 4}; env/invalid-measurement joins their permittedDeclineReasons. The README tracing list names G-03 / G-81 / WP-F3.
expectationHistory.why: Under the structural sum (0.6.0 with WP-F1) both blocks are reported (exit 1). WP-F3 round 2 declines a split block with a flow hazard, and that decline counts against the error rule's floor of 1 (exit 4). Neither mustFire entry would hold with certainty in a release that documents WP-F3, so each is recategorised with its reasoning instead of guessed. The construction truth (a defect) is unchanged.
expectationHistory.source: independent pre-run review (no breaklint output seen)

expectationHistory.what:
The same WP-F3 round 2 check applied to the corpus's other unbreakable-block candidates. required: false env/invalid-measurement declines were added for:
- sa03: the 19 rows of #tbl-stops on the landscape page, which reach past the portrait sheet (right edge 1065.8 px against 793.7 px).
- sa12: the 11 rows of #tbl-budget, likewise (998.4 px against 816 px).
- sa16: the two-fragment #signoff-sheet (table-columns) and its overflow-column row #so-42 (x = 1888 px on an 816 px sheet).
sa03's expectedExit becomes {1, 3, 4} and sa16's {0, 1, 3, 4}; env/invalid-measurement joins the permittedDeclineReasons of sa03 and sa16. The mustFire and mustNotFire entries of these documents are unchanged.
expectationHistory.why: WP-F3 round 2 declines an unsplit block that reaches past the sheet, and a split block with a flow hazard, whatever its fragment count. On a named landscape page Paged.js 0.4.3 keeps the portrait sheet, so every full-width row there reaches past it, under all three font stacks. Each such decline leaves the error rule's coverage below 1, so these documents can end in exit 4 in a release that documents WP-F3.
expectationHistory.source: corpus author during errata round 3, extending review item L4 to every unbreakable-block candidate of the corpus (no breaklint output seen)

expectationHistory.what: The why of the three {"id": "span-en"} mustNotFire entries (sa06 type/spaced-hyphen and type/straight-quotes, sa15 type/spaced-hyphen) now says the entry can never match. The inline span gets no source id, so a finding in it carries the range of the enclosing paragraph (sa06 #p-6-3, sa15 #p-r2-2). Such a finding is caught by the document-wide mustNotFire, which does not except that paragraph. The README's id row says the same.

expectationHistory.what: The release-semantics rule (README and manifest.json releaseSemantics) now reads 'is not measured by block, line or page rules (docs/limitations.md, the \'Margin-box content.\' bullet; the type rules still read a running element\'s source text once, and SVG in a margin box is still collected)' in place of 'is not measured by any rule (docs/limitations.md \'unmeasured margin-box content\')'. The why and docsBasis of the 80 running-element mustNotFire entries use the same wording and anchor. Checked on the static HTML: none of the 16 running elements contains SVG, a straight quotation mark or a spaced hyphen.

previous.releaseSemantics: Expectations follow the documented semantics of the breaklint release that admits this corpus (0.7.0): e.g. content in Paged.js margin boxes (running()/fixed copies) is not in the flow and is not measured by any rule (docs/limitations.md 'unmeasured margin-box content'); layout/orphaned-continuation-page judges a page only where its content ends; layout/unbreakable-block-too-tall correlates fragments by flow membership, not coordinates.

expectationHistory.source: independent pre-run review (no breaklint output seen)

expectationHistory.question: Q1
expectationHistory.what: README Targets table defines {"svg": X, "id": T}, used by the eight SVG mustFire entries: a finding matches when its source lies within the span of the <text> element T, and X is T's nearest <svg> ancestor. The gate's reading is confirmed: AND, with matching by T's span. Checked on the static HTML for all 422 text and <use> ids in svg targets: each has the named svg as its nearest <svg> ancestor (the nested viewport of sa17 included). A gate that finds otherwise fails the entry. No expected file and no document changed; no truth value changed.
expectationHistory.why: The shape was used but not defined.
expectationHistory.source: gate author's specification questions (WP-K2), ruled from the specification's intent (no breaklint output seen)

expectationHistory.question: Q2
expectationHistory.what: README paragraph 'Evidence-level declines': notMeasured rows with ruleId null are outside the corpus's closed world. The build emits two such reasons (src/render/evidence.ts): env/evidence-fragment-outside-page (scope page) and env/evidence-overlay-removed (scope document). A gate leaves these rows out of every per-rule check (the decline counts and permittedDeclineReasons). It fails a ruleId-null row with any other reason or scope. The exit check is not exempt. Gate step 5 (and so manifest.json gate.steps) now limits the permittedDeclineReasons check to the rule's own rows. No expected file and no document changed; no truth value changed.
expectationHistory.why: These rows say whether the evidence overlay could be bound to the rendered PDF, which depends on the rasteriser, the evidence options and the environment, not on what a rule measured in the construction. The construction probe does not model evidence binding, so the corpus has no truth to state about them. Step 5's wording would have failed every document in CI, where evidence binding is on.
expectationHistory.previous: step 5: 'no decline carries a reason outside permittedDeclineReasons'
expectationHistory.source: gate author's specification questions (WP-K2), ruled from the specification's intent (no breaklint output seen)

expectationHistory.question: Q3
expectationHistory.what: README section 'Field list': a closed list of keys for every level of an expected file (top level, language, paper, pages, expectedExit, runningElements, constructionFacts, rules, the four entry lists, perText, targets and their shapes, uri, pageOf, except, verification and its sub-objects). Each key is marked normative (interpreted by a gate) or informational (presence and type only); measured, platformFonts and the inset objects are declared opaque. The previously unnamed informational keys (construction, text, observed, future, underContentExtentLowerBound, the verification sub-keys) are now listed with their meaning. The generator asserts the same list over all twenty files. No expected file and no document changed; no truth value changed.
expectationHistory.why: Without a closed list, the gate's 'unknown field fails' rested on the frozen files rather than on the specification.
expectationHistory.source: gate author's specification questions (WP-K2), ruled from the specification's intent (no breaklint output seen)

expectationHistory.question: Q4
expectationHistory.what: README: the value compared by a uri or id target of artifact/local-uri is the attribute value as the HTML parser returns it, with character references decoded and nothing else changed (no trimming, resolution or normalisation). No URI-bearing attribute in the corpus contains a character reference, so decoded and authored bytes coincide. srcset is out of scope: no document has a srcset, poster or data attribute, no target names one, and the id-target attribute list no longer mentions srcset candidates. No expected file and no document changed; no truth value changed.
expectationHistory.why: 'Raw (authored)' was ambiguous against a parser that decodes entities, and the message form of a srcset candidate was undefined.
expectationHistory.previous: 'raw (authored) value'; id targets listed 'each srcset candidate'
expectationHistory.source: gate author's specification questions (WP-K2), ruled from the specification's intent (no breaklint output seen)

expectationHistory.question: Q5
expectationHistory.what: README confirms three points and states them normatively. pages.range is inclusive at both ends (gate step 4 and the Field list). Every id a target names occurs exactly once in its document, and a target naming a duplicated or missing id fails its entry (checked: no document has a duplicate id; every targeted id exists). E17's rule applies per list: within one list of one rule no target repeats (in expectedDeclines, target together with reason). Across one rule's lists, mustFire, mustNotFire and allowed share no target (checked), and a mustFire or allowed target may also appear in expectedDeclines. No expected file and no document changed; no truth value changed.
expectationHistory.why: The gate author had assumed these; the README did not state them.
expectationHistory.source: gate author's specification questions (WP-K2), ruled from the specification's intent (no breaklint output seen)
